COVID-19 Intensive Care Occupancy in Bavaria

Source: R/data.R
icu_bavaria.Rd

Daily number of COVID-19 patients in adult intensive care units in Bavaria, Germany, with the reported first admissions and the infections reported in the previous seven days, from 20 March 2020 to 31 December 2023.

Usage

icu_bavaria

Format

A data frame with 1382 rows, one per day, and 4 columns:

date

Date of the report.

occupancy

COVID-19 patients in adult intensive care (faelle_covid_aktuell in the register).

admissions

First admissions of COVID-19 patients to intensive care that day (faelle_covid_erstaufnahmen); NA before 29 July 2021, when the register started recording them. Patients moved between intensive care units are not first admissions.

cases7

Laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infections in Bavaria, all ages, reported in the seven days up to and including date (Faelle_7-Tage).

Source

Robert Koch-Institut (2026). Intensivkapazitaeten und COVID-19-Intensivbettenbelegung in Deutschland, version of 8 November 2026. Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.24053879 . Robert Koch-Institut (2026). COVID-19 7-Tage-Inzidenz in Deutschland, version of 9 November 2026. Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.24074082 . Both are licensed under CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Changes: rows for Bavaria and all ages only, dates up to 31 December 2023, four columns kept and renamed. The script data-raw/icu_bavaria.R in the package repository rebuilds the data from the sources.

Details

The day-to-day change in occupancy is the number of patients who entered intensive care minus the number who left it (discharged, moved to a normal ward, or died), two counts that were not published for most of the pandemic. Modelled as independent Poisson counts, their difference has a Skellam distribution (Rave and Kauermann, 2025). Since 29 July 2021 the register also reports first admissions, which can be used to check the admissions estimated from the occupancy alone; see the article Disease surveillance on the package website.

References

Rave, M. and Kauermann, G. (2025). The Skellam distribution revisited: Estimating the unobserved incoming and outgoing ICU COVID-19 patients on a regional level in Germany. Statistical Modelling 25(3), 270-288. doi:10.1177/1471082X241235024

Examples

head(icu_bavaria)
#>         date occupancy admissions cases7
#> 1 2020-03-20        61         NA   2967
#> 2 2020-03-21        67         NA   3580
#> 3 2020-03-22        82         NA   4459
#> 4 2020-03-23        94         NA   4851
#> 5 2020-03-24       123         NA   5305
#> 6 2020-03-25       132         NA   6048

# the daily change in occupancy: admissions minus departures
change <- diff(icu_bavaria$occupancy)
c(mean = mean(change), variance = var(change))
#>         mean     variance 
#>   0.07892831 157.83072233 

# both rates over the first quarter of 2022, from the changes alone
z <- subset(icu_bavaria, date >= as.Date("2022-01-01") & date < as.Date("2022-04-01"))
fit <- skellam.fit(diff(z$occupancy))
coef(fit)
#>  lambda1  lambda2 
#> 102.5985 105.2389 
mean(z$admissions)   # reported first admissions per day
#> [1] 37.36667
# The estimated rates are far higher: without covariates, every source of
# day-to-day variation (transfers between units, reporting delays) counts as
# admissions and departures. The article shows how a model in which
# departures are proportional to occupancy recovers the reported admissions.
